newsitem.title: USA: UPS pilots warn of separate strike around Christmas.
newsitem.headline: UPS pilots warn of separate strike around Christmas.

text.p: The head of the union representing pilots at United Parcel Service said Thursday that a strike against the company by its pilots was possible near Christmas.

"A strike could potentially occur close to Christmas," Independent Pilots Association President Robert Miller told a news conference. IPA members are already honoring the Teamsters union strike against the giant package delivery company by refusing to fly UPS planes.
About 2,000 members of the Independent Pilots Association normally work for UPS flying its fleet of 500 aircraft. They had been working without a contract since December 1995.
Talks between the pilots and UPS have been on hold after a federal mediator ordered a recess in June. This "cooling-off" period is slated to end soon and talks could resume in September.
Miller said UPS pilots were paid 25 percent less than pilots at competing delivery service Federal Express Corp. and 33 percent below the rest of the industry.
"I can only say to you - 'Do we want back to back strikes?'" he said.
